function: No learned component performs the physical-layer function: PSO chooses power, amplitudes and STAR-RIS element split; the DNN only predicts the ergodic rate as an objective surrogate (pp. 6-8).
notes: Excluded as no_learning, a borderline case. The paper is a closed-form outage and ergodic-rate analysis (pp. 5-6) plus PSO optimization of power allocation, amplitudes and STAR-RIS element partitioning (p. 6), and JPRTE-SOP uses no learning. Only JPRTE-ESR uses ML: a 22-input, two-hidden-layer DNN trained on 50,000 samples of the analytical rate of Eq. (14), with one output neuron "to predict the ER of Ur*" (p. 7), after which "the PSO Algorithm 1 is now used to maximize" the predicted sum rate (p. 8). The DNN replaces evaluating a closed-form expression to cut runtime (Table III, p. 11, 2.95 s against 179.45 s); it outputs no configuration, so the decision is made by a classical iterative algorithm. If the reviewer counts this surrogate as part of the RIS configuration method, area 3 would apply, with q1=0 (custom Nakagami-m channels, p. 4), q2=0, q3=0 (only non-learned AO, FPRTE, conventional RIS, analytical-PSO and exhaustive search, pp. 9-11), q4=1 (runtime, Table III, p. 11) and q5=0 (no code or data link). Table III was read from the page image.
